steps.body:
A differential equation does not tell you what y IS. It tells you, at every point, **which way to go**.

dy/dx = f(x, y) is an instruction: *at this point, leave with this slope.*

Draw a tiny segment at every point with the prescribed slope and you have a **slope field** — a set of instructions. A solution is any curve that obeys them everywhere.
Thread a curve through the instructions.

widget.prompt: dy/dx = x. Drag the starting value to y = 5, and watch the curve thread through the field.
widget.successFeedback: Look at the field: the segments depend only on x, so every column is identical. That means every solution is just a VERTICAL SHIFT of every other — which is the + C from C4, drawn. Slide the starting value up and down and watch the same curve slide with it.
widget.lowFeedback: Below 5. Keep dragging up — and notice the curve's SHAPE never changes as you do.
widget.highFeedback: Above 5. Come back down — and notice, again, that only the height changed.

cml.actionGoal: Change an initial condition and trace a solution that remains tangent to the local direction field.

predict.prompt: dy/dx = x — the slope depends on x alone. Start two curves at different heights. Compared with each other they will be…

options.label: The same shape, one sitting above the other
Different at first, then crossing somewhere

predict.reveal: The same shape, shifted. Every point in a vertical column has the same slope, because x is the same all the way up it — so the whole family is one curve translated up and down. That translation is the + C, and this is the picture it has been standing in for.

explanationVariants: dy/dx = x says the slope depends only on x. At x = 2 the slope is 2, no matter what y is — so every segment in that column is identical.
That is why every solution of dy/dx = x is a vertical shift of the others: the instructions never mention y.

widget.prompt: For dy/dx = x, what is the slope of the field at the point (2, 7)?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the y-coordinate. The equation says dy/dx = x, and it never mentions y at all.
That is 7/2. The equation is not a ratio of the coordinates; it says the slope IS x.
That is xy. Read the equation literally: dy/dx = x.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Read dy/dx = x literally: the slope equals the x-coordinate, so at x = 2 it is 2.
widget.successFeedback: Right. Every segment in the column x = 2 has slope 2, which is exactly why the solutions are vertical shifts of one another.

explanationVariants: Every starting point has exactly ONE curve through it, and there are infinitely many starting points — so infinitely many solutions. The initial condition picks one.
That is precisely the + C: the general solution is a whole family, and one extra fact selects a member of it.

widget.prompt: How many curves obey the instructions of a slope field?

options.label: Infinitely many — one through every starting point. The initial condition picks one.
options.feedback: Right, and that is the + C, drawn. The differential equation gives the FAMILY; the initial condition selects the member.

options.label: Exactly one.
options.feedback: Drag the starting value in the widget and a different curve appears each time. Every one of them obeys the same instructions.

options.label: None, until you solve it algebraically.
options.feedback: The curves exist whether or not you can write them down — the field defines them. Many differential equations have solutions that no formula can express.

options.label: Two — one going each way.
options.feedback: Each starting point gives one curve, traced both forward and backward. Different starting points give different curves.

steps.body:
So this is the picture the + C has been waiting for.

**The differential equation gives the FAMILY.** (the field)
**The initial condition selects ONE.** (the starting point)

And the field exists even when no formula does. Most differential equations cannot be solved with symbols at all — but their slope fields can always be drawn, and their curves always exist.

explanationVariants: dy/dx = 0.5y depends on y, so the slope changes as you move UP the page — the segments get steeper the higher you go. That is what exponential growth looks like as an instruction.
A field that mentions y is one where the solutions are NOT vertical shifts of each other — they fan out.

widget.prompt: For dy/dx = 0.5y, what happens to the field as you move upward (larger y)?

options.label: The segments get STEEPER — the bigger y is, the faster it grows.
options.feedback: Right, and that sentence IS exponential growth: the rate of growth is proportional to how much you already have.

options.label: They get flatter.
options.feedback: The slope is 0.5y, which grows WITH y. Bigger y, steeper segment.

options.label: Nothing changes.
options.feedback: That would be true if the equation mentioned only x. This one mentions y, so height matters.

options.label: They turn downward.
options.feedback: For positive y the slope 0.5y is positive, so the segments point up — and increasingly steeply.

steps.body: Match the field to the equation.
hints: Ask what the slope depends on. If the equation mentions only x, every column is identical.
If it mentions only y, every ROW is identical — the slope depends on how high you are, not how far along.
dy/dx = 2 gives the same slope everywhere: a field of parallel segments.
explanationVariants: dy/dx = 2 prescribes slope 2 at EVERY point, so the field is a set of parallel segments — and the solutions are the parallel lines y = 2x + C.
The number of distinct slopes in a field tells you what the equation depends on. A constant field means a constant equation.

widget.prompt: Match each equation to what its field looks like.

right.label: each COLUMN identical; steeper to the right
each ROW identical; steeper higher up

pairErrors.feedback: dy/dx = x depends on x, so it is the COLUMNS that are identical — the slope changes as you move right, not as you move up.
dy/dx = y depends on y, so it is the ROWS that match — the slope changes with HEIGHT.

widget.missFeedback: Ask which variable the right-hand side mentions. That is the one the slope varies with.
widget.successFeedback: Mentions neither → parallel. Mentions x → columns match. Mentions y → rows match. The field is a picture of the equation.

steps.body: An equation that tells a curve which way to go.
takeaways: dy/dx = f(x, y) is an INSTRUCTION at every point, and a solution is any curve that obeys it.
There are infinitely many solutions — one per starting point — and the initial condition picks one. That is the + C, drawn.
The field exists even when no formula does. Most differential equations cannot be solved with symbols; their curves exist anyway.
steps.teaser: Next: the one curve that never moves at all.

concept.body: Read the right-hand side as a command: *at this point, head off with THIS slope.* Draw the command as a little segment at every point, and a solution is any curve that follows the segments wherever it goes.

explanationVariants: dy/dx = y at the point (0, 3) says: leave with slope 3.
Substitute the point into the right-hand side.

widget.prompt: For dy/dx = y, what slope does the field prescribe at the point (0, 3)?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the x-coordinate. The equation says the slope IS y, which is 3 here.
